maria: Anyone else seeing annotations from global.values merging into workload annotations and causing scheduler mis-sched? I noticed GPUs getting scheduled with `nvidia.com/gpu` nodeSelector removed but annotation `gpu-required: true` stuck.
jonathan: yep, saw it in canary last night, chart uses `{{ merge .Values.global.annotations .Values.worker.annotations }}` which flattens everything.
sasha: merge will overwrite keys but if you pass nil maps it can copy old ones. Can you paste values.yaml?
maria: paste snippet:
```
global:
  annotations:
    gpu-required: "true"
worker:
  annotations: {}
```
# helm helper snippet
{{- define "common.annotations" -}}
{{- $ann := merge .Values.global.annotations .Values.worker.annotations -}}
{{- toYaml $ann | nindent 8 -}}
{{- end -}}
```
kevin: ah, the helper uses `merge` from sprig. In Helm v3 merge can behave unexpectedly with nil/empty maps. Use `default` with an empty dict, or build maps explicitly.
jonathan: suggested fix:
```
{{- $global := default (dict) .Values.global.annotations }}
{{- $worker := default (dict) .Values.worker.annotations }}
{{- $ann := merge $global $worker }}
```
maria: I tried that, lint still fine but Flux apply fails because our CRD rejects unknown annotation keys on workloads.
sasha: we should also add a values.schema.json to disallow top-level unknowns for worker.annotations, and add a unit test to chart-testing that renders with empty maps.
kevin: Also consider not merging annotations that are k8s-scheduler related. Maybe namespace them `redwood.io/gpu` to avoid collisions with other infra.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy of `inference-worker` aborted: GitOps detected mismatch in resource annotation set (rolling back). :warning:
jonathan: I'll open a quick PR to change helper to default dict + merge, add schema entry, and add a chart-test case. Assigning to me.
maria: thanks. Also file a follow-up to scrub old annotations from old releases via a k8s job.
kevin: +1. I'll add a small script to the ops repo to cleanup.
jonathan: PR link will be in a bit.
maria: :thumbsup:
